See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. ## Current single-container installations

Use [the standalone installation guide](standalone.md#run-one-installation-container)
for the current path: one container, three parent and nine child worker processes,
one server, and separate governed records per node. Each container launch starts
stopped for inspection. One installation's lifecycle controls all of its workers.
There is no Docker-in-Docker requirement and no separate DNS container.

Multiple installations must still have distinct storage roots, names, ports, and
operator sockets. Do not share an active node database between installations.
Their API queues are independent; common provider credentials can still share
quota and produce concurrent calls across installations. Codespaces remote
execution of the new path requires an actual acceptance run.

## Retained Compose and gateway compatibility

The remaining instructions document earlier single-record Compose installations
and optional hostname gateways. Their exact volume protections still apply when
maintaining one of those installations. They are not the default one-container
node runtime.

Each installation has its own record, secrets, configuration, and lifecycle.
The same source checkout may build many installations. The retired GitHub executor retains its historical records; matching versions
do not imply matching data.
No container needs GitHub Pages, Actions, public snapshots, or another project.
External AI access is needed only when an external provider is selected.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Shared source code] --> A[Install A]
  S --> B[Install B]
  S --> H[Hosted install]
  A --> RA[(A record)]
  B --> RB[(B record)]
  H --> RH[(Hosted record)]
```

WAKE✳︎ GOVERNANCE
================

This module is the mechanical rulebook for WAKE✳︎.

The model is allowed to PROPOSE changes to durable state.
It is never allowed to decide whether those changes are valid.

That distinction is central to the experiment:

    model output = proposal
    governance = authority
    durable state = accepted history

The functions in this file are deliberately deterministic. Given the same
state and the same proposal, governance should reach the same decision
regardless of which model produced the proposal.

A model cannot persuade this module, reinterpret its instructions, waive a
requirement, or edit the rules during an invocation.

A research transition is atomic: an invalid research action rejects that
transition without partial writes. application_policy.py owns the separate
editorial wrapper, which can withhold an invalid final blog while committing
independently valid research. Do not move that exception into the reducer.

This gives WAKE✳︎ an important property:

    failure can become durable information
    without failure becoming durable state.
"""
